newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine deputies start final '97 budget reading.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine deputies start final '97 budget reading.

text.p: Parliament in Ukraine began a final reading of the former Soviet republic's much-delayed 1997 budget on Friday, whose approval is a key step towards qualifying for a $2.5-$3 billion International Monetary Fund (IMF) loan.
Deputies banned the use of central bank credits to finance the deficit and removed a clause from the draft which would have limited foreign borrowing to $4.345 billion.
"We are here to vote for the budget today," Speaker Olexander Moroz, who has urged deputies to approve the draft before the constitution's first anniversary on Saturday, said.
Deputies have approved revenues of 22.39 billion hryvnias ($12.1 billion) and expenditures of 28.12 billion hryvnias.
The deficit has been set at 5.7 percent of gross domestic product or 4.0 percent by IMF standards.
The central bank wants the deficit to be covered using revenues from the Treasury-bill market and foreign credits, which are expected to cover 2.4 billion hryvnias of the deficit.

The draft budget, which was approved by the IMF and gained initial approval from parliament last December, forecasts annual inflation of about 25 percent -- but top government officials have forecast price growth at about 17 percent.

Only two of a package of nine tax reform laws underpinning the budget, on value-added tax and taxation of business profits, have been passed and the rest are to be considered after parliament reconvenes in September.
Budgets are supposed to be passed by January 1 according to the constitution but Ukraine has not passed a budget on time since it won independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.
Parliament plans to start debating next year's budget in September in a bid to avoid the record delays this year.
